item.title: Blanche on track to become attorney general after Cassidy endorsement
item.description: Republican Sen. Bill Cassidy on Friday endorsed Todd Blanche for attorney general, putting President Trump's former personal lawyer one step closer to the nation's top law enforcement role. CBS News congressional reporter Taurean Small has more.

item.title: Student athletes discuss how they view the future of college sports
item.description: President Trump is urging Congress to pass the Protect College Sports Act, which would establish new guidelines and protections for name, image and likeness payments and regulate things like the transfer portal. Student athletes Ella Brooks, Henry Gibbs, Temple Landry and Ruben Rojas Betanzos join "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: U.S. targets Iran's banking system, companies with new sanctions
item.description: This is the eighth round of Iran-related sanctions announced by the Trump administration this year.

item.title: Trump faces disappointing July jobs report
item.description: The economy unexpectedly lost 23,000 jobs in July, signaling a slowdown that could complicate the Federal Reserve's next move on interest rates in September. The Trump administration downplayed the jobs report, blaming it on federal downsizing and layoffs in World Cup hospitality. CBS News business producer Emily Pandise has more.

item.title: From Iran's Evin Prison, U.S. citizen Reza Valizadeh releases audio update
item.description: CBS News received a second audio message from journalist Reza Valizadeh, who's been held in Iran's notorious Evin Prison since 2024. He gave an update on the prison conditions and on fellow American Kamran Hekmati, believed to be suffering from a recurring cancer.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy's psychiatrists testify at her murder trial
item.description: Psychiatrists who treated Lindsay Clancy​ before she killed her children in Massachusetts testified at her trial Friday.

item.title: U.S. economy unexpectedly loses 23,000 jobs in July
item.description: The U.S. economy saw an unexpected 23,000 job losses for the month of July. CBS News MoneyWatch correspondent Kelly O'Grady has the details.

item.title: Wisconsin gubernatorial hopeful David Crowley says he's a "get stuff done Democrat" ahead of primary
item.description: Francesca Hong is leading the Democratic primary for Wisconsin governor, but the democratic socialist is not endorsed by Sen. Bernie Sanders or Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. One of her opponents, Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, joins to discuss his campaign.

item.title: Tennessee farmer discusses primary victory over Trump-backed Ogles
item.description: Republican Rep. Andy Ogles of Tennessee, backed by President Trump, lost his primary race to farmer Charles Hatcher in a redrawn district. Hatcher joins "The Takeout" to discuss his victory and to look ahead to November's general election.

item.title: Analysis of Trump's potential deal with Iran as he threatens more strikes
item.description: Robert Murrett, a retired vice admiral in the U.S. Navy and a professor at Syracuse University, joins CBS News to offer his analysis of President Trump's remark that a deal with Iran could come soon, and more.

item.title: Details on Oman's potential Strait of Hormuz deal; Iranian prisoner describes poor conditions
item.description: Sources tell CBS News that Iran and Oman continue to negotiate the terms of a potential deal regarding transit in the Strait of Hormuz. CBS News chief foreign affairs correspondent and "Face the Nation" moderator Margaret Brennan joins with more.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis escalate deadly attacks on Saudi-backed troops
item.description: Yemen's Houthi rebels launch fresh attacks on Saudi-backed government troops, says Yemeni state media, as Cruz says Trump must seek "regime collapse."

item.title: Appeals court blocks Trump's White House ballroom, teeing up Supreme Court fight
item.description: A federal appeals court said the White House lacks the authority to unilaterally construct the 90,000-square-foot ballroom. President Trump said the administration will appeal to the Supreme Court.

item.title: Trump says he'll appeal to Supreme Court after judges block White House ballroom construction
item.description: An appeals court on Friday barred President Trump from building a White House ballroom without congressional approval. Mr. Trump now says he'll take the case to the Supreme Court. CBS News senior White House and political correspondent Ed O'Keefe reports.

item.title: Senate scrambles to finish business ahead of summer recess
item.description: The Senate is speeding toward summer recess, clearing Todd Blanche's path to attorney general and approving new energy sanctions aimed at Russia on Friday. CBS News congressional correspondent Nikole Killion has the latest on what's left on the upper chamber's agenda.

item.title: July jobs report reveals unexpected loss of 23,000 jobs
item.description: Friday's jobs report showed employers shed jobs last month, rather than adding 95,000 new hires that had been forecast by economists.

item.title: A quandary for the Fed: Dealing with hot inflation and cool job growth
item.description: A sudden slump in hiring has dramatically changed the outlook for the Federal Reserve's September interest rate decision.

item.title: Idaho shooting video shows gunman start deadly rampage in In-N-Out drive-thru
item.description: Three people were killed in the shooting that started at an In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls, Idaho.

item.title: Pentagon releases new batch of UFO files: "Did you see that?"
item.description: The Pentagon on Friday released a new batch of documents and images related to UFOs, the fifth disclosure in recent months about the strange encounters.

item.title: "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" guests for Aug. 9, 2026
item.description: This week's guests include NIH Director Dr. Jay Bhattacharya, Republican Sen. Bill Cassidy and independent Sen. Bernie Sanders.

item.title: DOJ's top prosecutor in LA hires aide with pending battery charge, DUIs
item.description: First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli hired former top aide Shawn Lewis to be a federal law enforcement liaison, though Lewis has three prior convictions for driving under the influence and a pending battery charge.

item.title: Trump announces $180 million to boost mining education
item.description: President Trump announced over $180 million in grants to boost educational programs for the mining industry, part of a bid to increase critical mineral production.

item.title: Watch: Pentagon releases 16 new UFO videos
item.description: The Defense Department released a fifth batch of UFO files on Friday, nearly one month after its fourth drop. These are all of the videos in the latest tranche.

item.title: Energy company sues data center over who should pay for AI buildout
item.description: At issue is who pays to expand energy infrastructure when a data center​​ needs as much electricity​ as a midsize city.

item.title: Cassidy backs Blanche for attorney general, clearing way for confirmation
item.description: Louisiana Sen. Bill Cassidy, a Republican, announced he will vote to confirm Todd Blanche for attorney general.

item.title: Water rationing begins in Puerto Rico amid drought crisis: "It's brutal"
item.description: Puerto Rico's massive rationing measure comes amid a severe drought on top of shortages due to infrastructure issues.

item.title: Inside the NYC supervised drug-use sites focusing on harm reduction
item.description: A 5-year-old experiment sanctioned by the city of New York, but not by the federal government, provide supervised sites for drug users. The goal is to reduce overdose deaths and street drug use, but some critics still have doubts about the process. CBS News' Anna Schecter reports.

item.title: Americans got their biggest raises in 40 years. Inflation took most of it.
item.description: The typical American's paycheck has grown faster since 2019 than in any stretch since the early 1980s. But prices climbed nearly as fast, swallowing about 80% of the wage increase.

item.title: Flesh-eating bacteria has killed 5 in Louisiana this year, officials say
item.description: A flesh-eating bacteria found in warm coastal waters is responsible for at least five deaths so far this year in Louisiana, state health officials reported Thursday.

item.title: Exercise: Your Insurance Policy for the Future
item.description: In this episode of Healthful, Norah O'Donnell is joined by her personal trainer and fitness expert, Kira Stokes. Since they started exercising together 12 years ago, Kira pushed Norah to lift heavier weights - something Norah initially resisted. Norah has since learned that you lose up to 8-percent of your muscle mass every decade after the age of 30. The two discuss the emotional connection between movement and mental health, how to get started exercising, and what about those weighted vests! Plus - Norah answers what her favorite and least favorite exercises are. We'd love to hear what topics you want to hear covered on Healthful. Text Norah at 202-217-1107.
